value.hook: When a read optimization introduces transient Busy/Unknown errors, or reviewing F232 recovery.
value.title: Busy reads need safety and retry eligibility

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Complements the existing consumer-cache, bounded-worker and spawn-handoff notes; this is the transient-error seam learned in #280.

When an optimization replaces a fallback read with Busy/Err, trace both safety and retry eligibility. Unknown must not become an empty pane list, absent process or dead-server witness. Revive's preliminary Boolean may stop waiting on an error, but its separate locked observation must still decide. Spawn failure is not death: F211 preserves later binding and parent handoff.

Propagation alone does not establish recovery. CodexBinder records Seen before probing and logs pane-query errors without restoring eligibility. An isolated one-shot error left the valid seat unbound through 30 unchanged ticks; an unrelated new thread triggered binding. This is F232, explicitly ruled a C34 follow-up, with a separate repair assigned to Silkworm. The regression should require recovery after release without another thread/row change, while preserving the existing no-launch quiet cadence.

For Busy cost claims, qualify the window: #280 skips reads without launches for five seconds, then preserves fork/backoff for a frozen holder. Its independent primed 50 ms timer fired in 53.23 ms; 30 Busy reads forked nothing. Final reviewer evidence, including the consumer matrix and skip mutant, is in `community/roles/reviewer/outputs/2026-11/20-verdict-pr-280-c8d2eab.dd.json`, commit `44e3442169df15dfea3dc5aa430e02a093decabe`.
